grade.first_issue: In the sufficiency proof, the assertion that a near-vertex cut can be repeated to force the minimum angle below θ does not explicitly account for Shan-Yu retaining the other child or prove finite termination. This is a minor, directly repairable omission under the 6-point category, not a Rule E central gap: repeatedly bisecting a chosen angle makes both children contain half that angle, so finitely many repetitions suffice.
grade.summary: The claimed classification is correct. Apart from the omitted adversarial justification in the initial small-angle reduction, the sufficiency argument is valid: the range analysis forces either θ or (n−1)θ, and a multiple kθ can then be peeled down to θ. The safe-angle invariant and four-case analysis in the necessity direction are correct and complete.
strengths: Correctly identifies exactly θ=180°/n for integers n≥2.
The cut-angle interval analysis and subsequent peeling of kθ are mathematically sound.
The necessity proof correctly establishes an invariant using all four possible pairs of newly created angles.

errors.description: The phrase “by repeating this” does not show why Shan-Yu cannot always discard the child with the small angle, nor specify a fixed decrement ensuring a finite number of cuts. A one-line angle-bisection argument repairs this.
